run_variance_observation.implication: Two nominally identical 200-step runs differ 6.7x in final train loss. Briefing SS LV: 'IF seed variance exceeds architecture difference: increase seeds before concluding.' The round-2 ranking that promoted evidence_bottleneck over span_port rested on step-6 losses (32.0 vs 81.3) from single runs; that separation has not been shown to survive run-to-run noise. Strengthens the BLOCKED verdict.

native_extended.superseded_value_note: TWO runs of the same run_id/seed exist across a training-loop change, both recorded in commit fb39282: (1) pod 3taen8m3jgcs7z @ 55547c3, final_loss 0.007259658, with its own runtime block (started 11:16:05, deleted 11:20:30, gpu_train_seconds 51, wallet 159.62->159.56); its weight pull hit CORRUPT_INTERRUPTED and the pod was deleted, so no weights survive. (2) pod nrejxttt2nuxfa @ d0165d8, final_loss 0.048755866, weights pulled and VERIFY_OK. The verified local checkpoint corresponds to run (2). Steps 6-160 are bit-identical across both records (same seed/data); only the tail diverges. Do NOT treat 0.007259 as unsupported - treat it as run (1), whose artifacts did not survive.

native_extended_caution.implication: 200 steps over 96 examples is ~34 epochs; the curve is non-monotonic and the final checkpoint is 1.84x worse than the step-160 minimum. Final train loss in this regime measures memorization, not capability, and must not by itself decide evidence_bottleneck vs span_port promotion (briefing SS XIV/LV). Rank on held-out P1 eval, not train loss.
